cards.title: One process, one GUI thread
items: the shipped container is a single Qt 6 process: a Widgets or QML shell on the GUI thread plus a worker pool for anything that can block
the GUI thread never blocks — no synchronous network, disk, parse or crypto; one-shot work rides QFuture/QtConcurrent, long-lived work a QObject on a QThread, bounded work a QThreadPool
the desktop holds a cache and an outbox; the backend stays the source of truth, and a server refresh replaces the local projection

cards.title: The local machine is untrusted
items: secrets live in the OS keystore behind SecretStorePort (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, libsecret); SQLite, config, logs and crash dumps hold none
OIDC + PKCE runs in the system browser with a loopback or custom-scheme redirect; the refresh token rotates with reuse detection
updates are signed, TLS is always on, and managed policy beats user settings — a kill switch applies immediately

cards.title: The three skills
items: qt-best-practices loads on every Qt edit and carries the stack contract digest (references/qt-architecture.md, qt6.md, qt-patterns.md, cpp-strict.md)
qt-review writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the file, the rule it breaks and the smallest fix; a broken architecture contract outranks everything
qt-port ports Qt 5, QML-only, PySide/PyQt, Electron or a web screen to Qt 6 C++, porting the original tests first

cards.title: The gates that keep the contract
items: lints/.clang-tidy (bugprone-, performance-, modernize-, readability-, a reviewed cppcoreguidelines- subset and qt-*) and lints/.clang-format are the copy-in unit; CI runs them --dry-run --Werror
lints/check/ holds deliberate violations next to a clean control, so the config proves it fires and the clean file stays quiet
CI runs four jobs: check-skill.py (frontmatter, links, manifests), check-examples.py (C++ block balance), the unittest suite under tests/, and check-build.sh + check-lints.sh on a pinned Qt toolchain
